title: Implement QAM modulation with soft-decision demapping
description:
Build a general modem framework for link simulation that supports arbitrary constellations and arbitrary bit mappings, while making common Gray-coded square QAM the optimized default path for production-style BICM workflows.

## Background

The current modulation surface is fragmented across `crates/gf2-coding/src/channel.rs` (BPSK + AWGN), `crates/gf2-coding/src/modulation.rs` (QPSK-only logic), and `crates/gf2-coding/src/fading.rs` (QPSK + Rician integration). That split was sufficient for the SOGRAND-era placeholder QPSK path, but it does not scale to DVB-T2-style QAM, custom research constellations, or accelerator-friendly batch demapping.

This epic replaces the placeholder QPSK implementation with a shared modem framework that separates constellation geometry, bit labeling, mapping, demapping, and channel composition. The framework must support arbitrary constellations for research ergonomics, while providing extremely fast Gray-coded square-QAM presets for QPSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM, and 256-QAM. CPU scalar + SIMD support is required in this epic; GPU work is tracked only as a conditional prototype branch.

Bit-channel analysis is also a requirement. Different bit positions inside one symbol can have different reliability, so the modem surface must support per-bit-channel LLR distribution and information-metric analysis without imposing overhead on simulations that do not request it.

Downstream story `003e4088` depends on this epic for the unified DVB-T2 FEC + QAM chain, so the resulting API must be ergonomic enough to slot into the existing simulation harness without bespoke glue.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] The crate exposes an ergonomic modem framework that supports arbitrary constellations and arbitrary bit mappings.
- [ ] Gray-coded square-QAM presets for QPSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM, and 256-QAM exist and are the optimized default path for common BICM workflows.
- [ ] Existing BPSK/AWGN and QPSK/Rician simulation flows run through framework-backed adapters rather than bespoke modem implementations.
- [ ] Soft-decision demapping is validated against reference formulas and tests for AWGN and the current fading use cases.
- [ ] Bit-channel analysis tools can evaluate per-bit LLR behavior and information metrics without penalizing non-analysis simulation paths.
- [ ] Benchmarks cover generic versus specialized modem paths, and the accelerator interface is ready for SIMD and future GPU backends.
- [ ] The downstream DVB-T2 integration story `003e4088` can consume the new modem surface without bespoke glue.

## Notes

Create child stories and leaf tasks that cover the modem core API, the arbitrary-constellation reference path, the Gray square-QAM fast path, simulation integration, migration of legacy modem surfaces, bit-channel analysis, public-facing validation and benchmarking, and a conditional GPU prototype path.
